chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Humayd, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have been assigned a task/position, is there a way out for me from that?' He said, 'Many are those who seek a way out from that, but it becomes difficult for them.' I said, 'What do you advise?' He said, 'I advise you to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and do not return (to it).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on exiting a appointed position or duty according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses a companion appointed to a specific office or duty who seeks a way out. The Imam observes that while many desire to escape such responsibilities, it often becomes burdensome, and thus advises him to maintain God-consciousness (Taqwa) and simply avoid returning to the role, suggesting a pragmatic approach to administrative duties where immediate resignation may be difficult. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual integrity with practical engagement in worldly affairs, provided one remains mindful of divine accountability.
